design:
Decided with the operator 2026-10-23: one vertical thread for the whole project, for anyone; knots are recursive (a knot opens into its own thread of finer knots); a new Thread tab beside Overview; the page opens at the present with a jump to the beginning; work outside any specification is on the thread too; the thread is drawn in madder. Built in order: a thread derived from records the Hub already links, then manager-authored chapters and summaries, then whatever gaps the first two reveal.

Changed 2026-10-23 (operator): the manager-chapters done-condition no longer says that disabling the job returns the structural surface. Chapters, once created, stay shown; the job's switch only decides whether new ones are written. Only the description of the outcome changed; nothing had been built against it.

open_questions.question: Which history is missing today? The operator knows of none yet; decided after the first slice is visible.

When does the manager re-write chapters (on each merge, on a schedule, on request), and what may it cost per firing? Answered in the manager-chapters document: on major events and a button, rewrites only when asked, no cap, cost shown.

problem: History in AgentWeave is recorded but scattered across per-object views and capped, newest-first lanes. Nobody can follow a project start to finish, and a business stakeholder cannot read it at all. The product's promise — nothing appears out of thin air — is not something a person can see.

in_scope: One thread through a project's whole history, in the app
non_goals: Acting on work from the thread
Replacing the Activity tab or per-object history views
Publishing the thread outside the app

slices.done: On the trial Hub, this repository's project shows a Thread tab whose surface reaches back to the project's first record, and opening a change knot down to a run knot ends at a link that opens that run's transcript.
slices.intent: Open the Thread tab and follow the project from its first record to now, opening any knot into finer knots down to links to the real objects.
slices.title: The thread from what is already recorded

slices.done: With the chapters job enabled, the Thread surface shows manager-written chapters whose every cited record exists, reaching back before the Hub's first record through git; disabling the job stops new chapters being written while those already written stay shown.
slices.intent: The surface reads as a story: the Hub's manager groups changes and other work into titled chapters with plain-language summaries that cite only real records.
slices.title: Chapters the manager writes

slices.done: Each gap the operator chose to close appears as knots on the thread for activity that happens after the slice ships.
slices.intent: Whatever the first two slices show the Hub never recorded (decided once they are visible) starts being recorded and appears on the thread.
slices.title: Record what the thread shows is missing

summary: Make the identity's red thread real in the app: one vertical thread through a project's entire history that anyone can read at the surface and anyone can pull down, knot by knot, to exactly what happened and who did it.
title: The red thread: a project's history you can pull
